Sort genes by residual normality and equality of variance

Source: R/test_norm.R
test_norm.Rd

For each gene, fits y ~ factor1 * factor2 * ... and tests the residuals for normality (Shapiro-Wilk) and the groups for equal variance (Levene, median- centered, groups = every combination of the factors). Genes are sorted into: ne: normal, equal variance (Shapiro p >= shapiro_threshold, Levene p >= levene_threshold) nu: normal, unequal variance (Shapiro p >= shapiro_threshold, Levene p < levene_threshold) nn: not normal (Shapiro p < shapiro_threshold) Missing values are dropped per gene. Shapiro-Wilk has little power with small groups (~8 samples per group), so many non-normal genes will still be sorted as normal. Constant genes should be removed beforehand.

Usage

test_norm(x, factors, shapiro_threshold = 0.05, levene_threshold = 0.05)

Arguments

x

a numeric data.frame or matrix, genes as rows

factors

a vector with one group label per column of x (one-way), or a data.frame with one column per factor (two-way and up)

shapiro_threshold

significance level for the Shapiro-Wilk test

levene_threshold

significance level for the Levene test

Value

a list with data.frames ne, nu, nn (subsets of x, original row order) and tests, a data.frame with per-gene shapiro and levene p-values and the assigned set. Levene is reported for every gene, but is only used to sort genes that pass Shapiro.
